# 319-sinterklaasavond

Second Sinterklaas liedje — the method-driven companion to #318. A gentler
"evening" liedje (G major, 100 BPM) whose **melody is generated by a real
composition method** and whose **audio is realized through a production
method**, instead of a hand-authored tune + plain FluidSynth.

- **Style**: `sinterklaas` · **Key**: G major · **Tempo**: 100 BPM · 4/4
- **Form**: Intro(4) → Verse(8) → Verse2(8) → Outro(4) = 24 bars (strophic)

## Composition method — 023 Tendency Masking (two-phase)

| Phase | What |
|---|---|
| **Phase 1** | `generators.tendency_masking.TendencyMaskingGenerator` emits a stochastic melody inside a moving **singable register envelope** (G4–F#5) — the "tendency mask" keeps a children's tune inside a singable corridor. 8th-note step, density 0.85. |
| **Phase 2** (rules) | strong beats (1 & 3) snap to the bar's **I–IV–V chord tone**; every note is re-clamped to the nearest scale pitch within a **3rd** of the previous (conjunct/singable); fully diatonic. |

Accompaniment is the style's rules layer (tuba oom-pah, celesta pad,
glockenspiel bell arp, light march) — the same framework as #318.

## Production method — SP-032 FDN Reverb

The humanized render goes through `sound.effects.fdn_reverb.FDN` (warm hall:
size 0.72, decay 0.62, brightness 0.45, wet 0.32) before the master pass. The
perfect render is left **dry** so the production method is A/B-able.

## Verification

- zero-drift ✓ · perfect off-grid 0 / humanized 350 ✓
- out-of-scale 0 (all diatonic G major) ✓
- melody range G4–E5, max consecutive leap = a **3rd** (conjunct) ✓
- master → −16 LUFS, −1 dBTP ✓
